newsitem.title: INDIA: Protests as Miss World beauty show opens in India.
newsitem.headline: Protests as Miss World beauty show opens in India.

text.p: Indian police kept tight security at the Miss World beauty contest on Saturday after violent protests in which about 1,500 people were detained and threats by militant women to commit suicide by immolation.
Police with blankets, water hoses and sniffer dogs were among 20,000 spectators in Bangalore's cricket stadium and maintained a lookout for women who had threatened to set themselves on fire.
"The chances of any woman bringing in material to burn herself are very slim," a senior police official said inside heavily-guarded Chinnaswamy stadium.
Mid-way through the show, with a theme of fire and Hindu ruins, there were no reported protests in the stadium itself.
In deference to Indian mores, the contestants wore long transparent skirts around their swimsuits.
The Miss World pageant has been dogged for more than two months by protesters who claim the beauty show is demeaning to women and undermines India's 5,000-year-old cultural heritage.
The first Miss World contest to be held in India opened with traditional music and the swirl of dancers on a set of reconstructed ruins of a 14th-century Hindu temple.
Organisers said the events would be seen by more than two billion television viewers worldwide.
Streets outside the stadium were almost deserted after the pageant opened. A few hours earlier, they had been filled with tear gas after stone-throwing protesters clashed with police.
Police said about 1,500 people were detained during a day of protests with strong political overtones and an earlier round-up of suspected troublemakers.
Police said they would probably be freed on Sunday after the Miss World contestants left for New Delhi, India's capital.
Up to seven policemen were injured, police said. Casualties among the protesters were not known.
Police and Miss World organisers remained alarmed by the threat of self-immolation by members of Mahila Jagran Samiti (Forum for Awakening Women), led by Kinay Narayana Shashikala.
Shashikala has been in hiding since Thursday but members of India's opposition Hindi nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said they were in contact with her.
She had said her followers would mingle with the spectators and set fire to themselves after first taking poison.
Last week, an unemployed man in southern India died after setting himself ablaze in protest against the pageant.
Hours before the start of the contest, three separate demonstrations led by right-wing Hindu nationalists left clouds of tear gas over roads leading to the outdoor stadium.
Police said three members of parliament from New Delhi and belonging to the BJP were among those held in protests.
The contest is being held in the capital of Karnataka, the home state of Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, whose 13-group centre-left coalition succeeded the BJP in June.
The right-wing BJP held office for only 12 days after general elections in April and May.
B.S. Yediyurappa, head of the BJP in Karnataka's state assembly, was also held. "I want the resignation of the state government. We are being denied our democratic rights," he said.
